newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* The Dow industrials, which rose by nearly 130 points during the day, saw the gains whittled away by day's end, closing up 50.97 points at 7,136.62.
* The Goldman, Sachs Retail Composite Index rose 3 percent in April over the prior year.
* A World Trade Organization panel has issued a preliminary ruling that the European Union's ban on hormone-treated beef is illegal.

* The WTO also has issued a preliminary ruling that the policy of guaranteeing Caribbean banana farmers special access to the European market is an unfair restriction on American companies that grow bananas in Latin America.
* Sony Corp's fourth quarter earnings jumped to 12.34 billion yen (US$99.5 million), or $0.23 a share, up from 1.03 billion yen (US$8.23 million), or $0.03 per share.
* A Food and Drug Administration panel has recommended rejection of an injection treatment for Lou Gehrig's disease that was developed by a partnership between Cephalon Inc and Chiron Corp.
* Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd BXM.TO won court protection from its creditors in the aftermath of accusations of perpetuating the largest mining swindle in history.

* Ford Motor Co and Associates First Capital Corp, a lending company majority owned by Ford, are reviewing allegations that Associates took advantage of poorly educated borrowers or those from low-income and minority groups.
* PNC Bank Corp is in talks to acquire the privately held Oppenheimer & Co Inc, the brokerage firm, for about $500 million, according to an unnamed source.
* International Business Machines Corp has agreed to buy the balance of its 70-percent owned Advantis computer services company from Sears, Roebuck & Co for $450 million.
* United Paramount Network Chairwoman and Chief Executive Lucie Salhany has decided not to renew her contract with the television network.
* The U.S. Commerce Department said it would allow in some cases the unlimited export of encryption products.
* Living Centers of America Inc and GranCare Inc said they have agreed to merge in a $1.8 billion deal that would create the second-largest long-term care provider in the United States.
* US Airways Group Inc said they plan to stop flying some of their most unprofitable routes, close some operations, ground nearly two dozen aircraft and layoff some pilots.

* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan defended the central bank's recent action raising interest rates, saying that the absence of the move would have been a threat to job security and standards of living for "too many Americans".
* Applebee's International Inc brings a hometown feel to its national chain of restaurants, becoming the United States' largest and fastest-growing casual-dining chain.
